Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page panel: top account banner, section cards (activity data / personalized ads / location / search / devices), each card with a toggle + "Details" link + "Delete my X data" button; prominent danger zones for Download my data and Delete account; privacy-policy links in the footer | | `styles.css` | Cards, toggle switches, warning colors (yellow / red), confirmation modal styles | | `script.js` | Toggle coordination, delete second-confirmation modal, form mock submission, status indicators |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full privacy-dashboard system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The privacy dashboard provides strong structural clarity and safe destructive action patterns, but suffers from severe mobile usability issues and a trapping details drawer. Critical interactive elements like checkboxes (16x16px), interest remove buttons (20x20px), and navigation links fall far below the 44px mobile tap target guidance. Additionally, the details drawer lacks responsive layout and keyboard support, causing users to become stuck, while the Privacy Checkup 'Start' button fails to initiate its flow.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the privacy dashboard, validating all primary privacy controls, data management flows, destructive actions, and responsive layout behavior.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will systematically traverse the dashboard's primary sections using the left navigation, starting with the Overview and Privacy Checkup. It will then validate the core privacy toggles and data deletion flows within Activity History and Data Controls, followed by Ad Personalization and App Access. Finally, it will test destructive and high-risk actions like Export Data and Account Deletion, ensuring modals and confirmations behave correctly, before re-verifying critical interactions on a mobile viewport.
assumptions: The dashboard is a single-page application where left navigation buttons dynamically update the main content area without full page reloads.
The 3 detected dialogs correspond to delete confirmations, data export status, or account deletion warnings.
Toggle switches and delete buttons trigger local state changes and mock submissions handled by script.js.
Small tap target warnings on desktop will likely exacerbate on mobile viewports, requiring specific validation.
risk_hotspots: Delete account / Delete my data buttons: Destructive actions must have clear confirmation dialogs and easy cancellation paths.
Toggle coordination: Toggling off activity saving settings should appropriately reflect in the UI state and privacy score without errors.
Mobile navigation: The left sidebar and top navigation links have small tap targets on desktop; these may overlap, collapse poorly, or become unusable on mobile.
Data Export flow: Mock submission should provide clear feedback (e.g., loading state, success message) to avoid user confusion.

phases.title: Overview & Privacy Checkup
phases.objective: Validate the initial dashboard state, privacy score, and the guided privacy checkup flow.
key_checks: Verify privacy score and recommendation count are visible on load.
Click 'Start' on Privacy Checkup and validate progression through checkup steps.
Interact with the 'Search Ctrl K' button to verify search overlay/behavior.
Click 'Open help' and 'Account menu' to ensure dropdowns/overlays open and close correctly.
exit_criteria: Privacy checkup flow initiated and completed/closed.

phases.title: Activity & Data Controls
phases.objective: Test the core privacy toggles and data management settings for activity history and data controls.
key_checks: Navigate to 'Activity history' and toggle activity saving settings off/on.
Verify 'Auto-delete' settings interaction (e.g., changing from 18 months to 3 months).
Navigate to 'Data controls' and interact with available toggles.
Click 'Delete my data' buttons within these sections and validate the second-confirmation modal.
Cancel and confirm the deletion modal to check both recovery paths.
exit_criteria: Activity saving toggles flipped and state changes observed.
Delete confirmation modal successfully triggered, cancelled, and confirmed.

phases.title: Ad Personalization & App Access
phases.objective: Validate adjacent privacy settings for ad preferences and third-party app permissions.
key_checks: Navigate to 'Ad personalization' and toggle settings, verify interests/sensitive categories UI.
Navigate to 'App access' and review the list of connected apps.
Revoke access for an app with broad permissions and verify UI update.
Navigate to 'Devices & locations' and verify device list and location history controls.
exit_criteria: Ad personalization toggled and interests reviewed.

phases.title: High-Risk Actions & Export
phases.objective: Test the prominent danger zones and data export functionality to ensure safe UX patterns.
key_checks: Navigate to 'Export data' and trigger the data export mock submission.
Validate form submission feedback (e.g., status indicators, success message).
Navigate to 'Settings' and locate the 'Delete account' danger zone.
Initiate account deletion and verify the presence and behavior of the final confirmation modal.
Ensure cancellation is easy and default-focused to prevent accidental deletion.
exit_criteria: Data export initiated and status indicator observed.
Delete account modal triggered, validated for safe UX, and successfully aborted.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Re-test critical flows and layout stability on a mobile viewport, addressing prescan tap target warnings.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and verify sidebar navigation behavior (hamburger menu or collapsible).
Validate top navigation tap targets (Account, Privacy, Data controls, Apps, Devices) for usability.
Repeat a toggle interaction (e.g., Activity history) to ensure controls are accessible and not obscured.
Trigger a delete confirmation modal on mobile to check layout and scrolling behavior.
exit_criteria: Tap target issues validated and documented.
Critical interaction (toggle + modal) successfully completed on mobile.

findings.user_goal: Manage and delete activity data on a mobile device
findings.problem: Activity item checkboxes have a tap target size of only 16x16px, making them incredibly difficult to accurately select on touch screens.
findings.evidence: Multiple layout warnings and interaction logs show checkboxes (e.g., ux-161, ux-164) are 16x16px, far below the 44px mobile guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Users will experience high frustration and frequent mis-taps when trying to select items for bulk deletion, potentially leading to accidental actions on the wrong data items.
findings.suggestion: Increase the checkbox tap target area to at least 44x44px using CSS padding or a larger custom checkbox component.

findings.user_goal: Close the details drawer and return to the main dashboard
findings.problem: The details drawer's close button is positioned outside the standard desktop viewport (x: 1636 on a 1440px screen) and cannot be scrolled to, trapping the user in the drawer view.
findings.evidence: Click failed for Close details: element is outside of the viewport. Clicking the button (ux-40) repeatedly timed out because it overflows the viewport width.
findings.why_it_matters: Users are forced into a dead-end where they cannot dismiss the panel using the primary close button, requiring them to find alternative escape routes like clicking sidebar navigation.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the drawer close button is positioned responsively within the viewport bounds (e.g., using `right: 16px` instead of a large fixed offset).

findings.user_goal: Dismiss the details drawer using keyboard navigation
findings.problem: The details drawer does not close when the Escape key is pressed, violating standard modal/drawer accessibility patterns.
findings.evidence: Pressing Escape did not close the details drawer; the 'Close details' button (ux-40) remained visible, indicating the drawer was still open.
findings.why_it_matters: Keyboard-only and assistive technology users rely on the Escape key to dismiss overlays. Without it, they may become completely stuck and unable to navigate away.
findings.suggestion: Add a keydown event listener for the Escape key to the details drawer that triggers the close action.

findings.user_goal: Remove ad personalization interests on a mobile device
findings.problem: The 'Remove' buttons for ad interests (e.g., Cloud storage, Travel) are only 20x20px, making them very difficult to tap on mobile devices.
findings.evidence: Interaction logs note that remove buttons (e.g., ux-92) are 20x20px, significantly below the 44px mobile tap target guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Users with motor impairments or those using touch screens will struggle to remove interests, leading to accidental taps or inability to manage their ad profile effectively.
findings.suggestion: Increase the tap target of the remove buttons to at least 44x44px, or make the entire interest chip clickable to trigger removal.

findings.user_goal: Initiate the Privacy Checkup step-by-step flow
findings.problem: Clicking the 'Start' button for the Privacy checkup results in no visible change or navigation, failing to initiate the step progression.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Start' button (ux-19) resulted in no visible change or navigation, failing to initiate the step progression.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect a clear transition when starting a guided flow. A dead button creates confusion about whether the feature is broken or if the user misunderstood the UI.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the 'Start' button triggers a visible state change, such as advancing to the first checkup step or expanding the checkup recommendations.

findings.problem: Clicking 'Save retention' provides no explicit confirmation message (e.g., toast or inline text) to reassure the user that the preference was saved.
findings.evidence: No explicit confirmation message (e.g., toast, inline success text) is visible in the current observation to clearly reassure the user that the preference was saved.
findings.why_it_matters: In a privacy-critical context, users need clear assurance that their data retention settings have been successfully updated to avoid anxiety about their data.
findings.suggestion: Display a brief, non-intrusive success toast or inline message like 'Retention preference saved' after the action completes.

findings.user_goal: Revoke app access via the confirmation dialog
findings.problem: The confirmation dialog uses 'Delete' as the confirm action label instead of 'Revoke', which mismatches the initiating 'Revoke access' action.
findings.evidence: The confirmation dialog uses 'Delete' as the confirm action label instead of 'Revoke', which might cause slight cognitive friction since the initiating action was 'Revoke access'.
findings.why_it_matters: Mismatched terminology introduces cognitive friction and may cause users to hesitate, wondering if 'Delete' implies deleting their account data rather than just revoking the app's access.
findings.suggestion: Align the confirmation button label with the initiating action by changing 'Delete' to 'Revoke' in the app access confirmation dialog.
